claims.text: Kubernetes 1.34 has no separate field for sidecars: an init container with restartPolicy: Always is treated as a sidecar that starts and remains running for the Pod's whole life, and is restarted if it exits.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Concepts > Workloads > Pods > Sidecar Containers (Sidecar containers and Pod lifecycle)

claims.text: The kubelet starts a sidecar before spec.containers and moves on once it is started: its process runs and no startupProbe is defined, or its startupProbe succeeded (a probe run only during startup). Started does not mean it accepts connections.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Sidecar Containers (started status, startupProbe); Pod Lifecycle > Container probes (startupProbe)

claims.text: Ordinary (regular) init containers run to completion, one after another in order, before the app containers start.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Concepts > Workloads > Pods > Init Containers

claims.text: On Pod termination the kubelet postpones terminating sidecar containers until the main application containers have fully stopped, then stops sidecars in reverse order of their appearance.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Sidecar Containers; Pod Lifecycle > Termination with sidecars

claims.text: Containers of one Pod share its network namespace (IP address and ports), so they reach each other on localhost/127.0.0.1; a listener bound to 127.0.0.1 is not reachable from outside the Pod.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Concepts > Workloads > Pods (Pod networking: containers communicate via localhost); k8s.l3.pod-network-model summary 5

claims.text: Caddyfile: bind 127.0.0.1 limits the listener to that address; respond may use placeholders such as {http.request.header.X-Client-Subject}; header_up sets a request header, here to {http.request.tls.client.subject}, written as CN=gateway-client.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: Caddyfile directives > bind, respond, reverse_proxy (header_up); Caddyfile concepts > placeholders

claims.text: In Caddy 2.10, the version this lab pins, reverse_proxy passes Host to an HTTPS upstream unchanged by default; {upstream_hostport} is the upstream's host:port; transport http tls_client_auth <cert> <key> presents a client certificate, tls_trust_pool file <pem> sets the CAs that verify the upstream.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: reverse_proxy > Headers (Host passed through), Placeholders (upstream_hostport), Transports > http (tls_client_auth, tls_trust_pool, tls_server_name default)

claims.text: Caddy uses the upstream address's host as TLS server name (sent at connection start) by default; a Caddy server with client authentication configured enables strict SNI-Host matching and answers a Host that differs from the TLS ServerName with 421 Misdirected Request.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: global options > servers > strict_sni_host (on automatically with client auth); reverse_proxy transport http tls_server_name; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-26 (421 observed in repo)

claims.text: A service mesh's controllers (programs running a control loop over API-server objects) typically add a proxy to each Pod as it is created, give each app's Pods a certificate (in many meshes named after the ServiceAccount), renew it, and configure every proxy from API-server objects.
